rules: Prefer a shared remote endpoint over a locally spawned process.
A local server runs as one process shared across agents; multiple hosts must not each spawn their own instance of the same server.
A local server is started by the plugin or skill that needs it, not eagerly at session start, so no process is running for a session that never uses it.
activationPolicy.note: Recorded from an explicit owner preference on 2026-08-04: local MCP processes were multiplying across hosts and costing CPU and memory for sessions that never invoked them. activationMode carries this per server. 'shared-remote' means the fleet talks to one hosted endpoint and starts nothing locally. 'on-demand-local' means a local process is permitted, but only invoked through an owning capability, and only when that capability is used. A local server that would be eagerly started by every host at session start does not satisfy this policy regardless of how its activationMode reads.

protocolRevisionNote: Every server carries a `protocol` block establishing which MCP revision it actually speaks, probed rather than assumed. This exists because `transport: "http"` stopped being informative once the 2026-07-28 revision made the core stateless: a 2025-11-25 server and a 2026-07-28 server are both 'http' and are not wire-compatible. `revision: null` is a legitimate recorded state meaning 'could not be established', and it must say why -- it is never a placeholder for an unchecked entry. Known revisions are listed in knownProtocolRevisions.

mcpServers.name: Descript

protocol.verification: Both server/discover and initialize returned HTTP 401. This endpoint refuses protocol negotiation before an interactive OAuth grant, so the revision cannot be established non-interactively. Deliberately left null rather than assumed.

mcpServers.notes: Optional editorial-finishing MCP (import, Underlord edits, publish share links). Import only privacy/redaction/claim-cleared working media. Every edit creates a new candidate and invalidates prior preflight, review, arbiter, verifier, and automated release evidence; output without locally checksumable bytes is PIPELINE_BLOCKED. Publishing requires explicit task authorization plus current automated PASS evidence for the exact shared bytes. Claude uses its native account connector while retaining canonical Product Demo Studio loose skills; Codex and reviewed native plugin adapters use the plugin-owned MCP. Never connect both in one session. No local MP4 export via API. Consumes media minutes and AI credits. Docs: https://help.descript.com/hc/en-us/articles/46056322186509

mcpServers.notes: Registered 2026-08-08 during the fleet repository standardization. The workspace lives at the fleet root (.repowise-workspace.yaml); awesome-mcp-servers (external fork) and .demo-workspace (not a repo) are deliberately excluded. Post-commit hooks keep member indexes fresh; `repowise status -w` / `doctor -w` report fleet health. Dashboard: `repowise serve` from the fleet root.

mcpServers.name: Appium Mobile (Android local, iOS remote)
mcpServers.credentialPolicy: none-in-config; no account, token, or API key is required. AI_VISION_ENABLED is deliberately left off, because it would require an external vision API key and the native element tree already provides locators.
mcpServers.providesCapabilitiesNote: mobile.android.local -- an Android emulator or attached device on the Windows host, driven through the MCP's embedded UiAutomator2 (omit remoteServerUrl). mobile.ios.simulated -- an iOS Simulator inside the VMware macOS guest, driven by passing remoteServerUrl for the guest's Appium 3.6.0 + XCUITest 12.3.1 on port 4723. Neither capability covers a physical iPhone or a real-hardware claim.

localProcessPolicy.note: Pinned to 1.92.0 rather than @latest so a re-resolve does not silently move the lab; see chrome-devtools for the pinned precedent and brave-search for the deliberately unpinned counterpart. The lightweight stdio provider may be registered persistently on hosts without package activation. It does not start the Android emulator or macOS guest; those expensive resources stay cold until Start-MobileLab.ps1 is invoked.

mcpServers.notes: Registered 2026-08-10. Windows-host only: it needs adb for Android, and its iOS half is a remote client to the macOS guest rather than a local driver, because Xcode and simctl do not exist on Windows. The guest address is DHCP-assigned by VMware NAT -- resolve it with `vmrun getGuestIPAddress` (Test-MobileLab.ps1 does) instead of hardcoding it. NO_UI is set per the package's own guidance to cut generated-UI token overhead.
